title: Bridging lender completes £200k loan for Leicester office scheme
summary:
A £200,000 commercial bridging loan has been arranged for the conversion of a Grade II listed former school in Leicester into six detached office units. The transaction was completed in 15 working days after a high street bank refinance application stalled.

title: Norwich estate agency opens second branch after 18 years
summary:
An independent Norwich estate agency has opened a second branch 18 years after launching its first office, marking a notable expansion for the family-run firm. Property Ladder, operated by brothers James and Ed Brooks, has established a new office on Patteson Road in the NR3 area of Norwich.

title: Eviction notices surge 27% ahead of Section 21 abolition
summary:
More than a quarter of tenants were served eviction notices in the month before the Renters' Rights Act came into force on 1st May, according to new data from property management platform COHO. Analysis of 150,000 tenancies shows eviction notices peaked at 27.1% of tenancies immediately before Section 21 no-fault evictions were abolished.

title: Reform proposes social housing reallocation policy
summary:
Nigel Farage has outlined Reform's approach to social housing allocation, proposing that migrant households currently in social housing be required to relocate to the private rental sector within three months. The policy does not detail how the private rental sector would absorb the potential influx of households.

The post Reform proposes social housing reallocation policy appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Vistry cuts house prices by up to 17% amid cash pressures
summary:
Major housebuilder Vistry has reduced prices on some properties by more than £100,000, with discounts reaching 17% as the company seeks to improve cash generation. Analysis by RBC found that of more than 1,200 properties listed by Vistry during May, the average discount was 8.4%.

title: UK house price growth forecast to slow to 0.7% in 2027
summary:
House price growth in the UK is expected to slow significantly over the next 18 months, with higher mortgage costs and a weakening economy dampening demand. The Item Club forecasts prices will rise by just 1.1% this year, followed by growth of only 0.7% in 2027.

The post UK house price growth forecast to slow to 0.7% in 2027 appeared first on PropertyWire.

title: Manchester house prices rise 63% in decade versus London’s 7%
summary:
Manchester has recorded the highest house price growth among major UK cities over the past decade, with values increasing 63% compared to London's 7%, according to new analysis by Rightmove. The data reveals a widening north-south divide in the property market.

title: Renting versus buying in prime London property market
summary:
High stamp duty rates of up to 19% for non-UK residents are prompting wealthy buyers to reconsider renting rather than purchasing in London's prime property market. The combination of £3.8 million to £5.7 million in tax on properties valued between £20 million and £30 million, plus annual running costs of £500,000 or more, has shifted the financial calculation for international buyers.

title: Cleaning disputes dominate tenancy deposit claims
summary:
Cleaning-related issues accounted for 29.37% of all tenancy deposit disputes in 2025, marking the fifth consecutive year that cleaning has been the primary cause of disagreement between landlords and tenants. Property damage ranked as the second most common reason for deposit claims at 18.42%, followed by rent arrears at 16.45%.

title: Central banks hold rates as Iran deal eases inflation
summary:
Central banks in the US and UK are expected to maintain interest rates this week following a Middle East peace deal that analysts predict will reduce inflationary pressures. The US Federal Reserve is forecast to hold its benchmark rate at 3.5% to 3.75% while the Bank of England is anticipated to hold at 3.75%.
